criterion_scores.reasoning: Non-retryable isolation, NotSent semantics, guard ordering all correct; high-severity regression: DNS/TLS connect failures escape unhandled.
All scoped pieces present and selftests real; _send lifecycle untested; latent bare-path cache gap.
Single guarded write path preserved; implicit shared mutable state undocumented.
Lean fix for a measured friction; minor list-concat inefficiency.
Give-up message fixed; but the escaping exception bypasses all diagnostic messaging and the _send docstring overpromises.

defects.why: connect() handler only catches _TRANSIENT; socket.gaierror (DNS) and ssl.SSLError (TLS) are plain OSError, so they escape unwrapped, are not NotSent, not retried, and crash — a regression from urllib which wrapped them in URLError, contrary to the stated purpose.

defects.quote: def fake_send(method, path, data, headers, timeout, reuse):
defects.why: selftest mocks _send wholesale, so the new socket-lifecycle code (connect, reuse/drop, settimeout) has no automated coverage.
module-global mutable connection with no lock and no documented single-threaded assumption.

defects.quote: for k in [k for k in cache if k.startswith(f"/{table}?")]:
defects.why: a cached bare-path GET (no query string) would never be invalidated; latent.

defects.quote: attempt = attempts                     # may have landed: fail loud on the first stall, as before
defects.why: reassigning the loop variable as an exit sentinel is non-obvious; a named flag reads clearer.

defects.quote: self._made_names = getattr(self, "_made_names", []) + [(table, name)]   # display casing, for review output
defects.why: list rebuilt by concatenation on every call; append in place.
